# Axis Bank FY25 Annual Report: Master Summary

Axis Bank delivered robust consolidated financial performance in FY25 with net profit of ₹28,055 crores, growing 6% year-on-year, though profitability was constrained by a 91% surge in provisions and contingencies to ₹7,759 crores. Standalone net profit reached ₹26,373 crores, while operating profit grew 13% to ₹42,105 crores. The bank maintained strong capital adequacy with a CET-1 ratio of 14.67%, up 93 basis points organically, and total CAR at 17.07%, positioning it well above regulatory requirements.

The balance sheet expanded steadily with total assets reaching ₹16,09,930 crores (9% growth) and deposits growing 10% to ₹11,72,952 crores, driven by 14% growth in term deposits. Advances increased 8% to ₹10,40,811 crores, with retail advances comprising ₹6,22,897 crores. Net Interest Income grew 8.93% to ₹54,348 crores, though Net Interest Margin compressed to 3.98% from 4.07%. Non-interest income rose 13% to ₹25,257 crores, with fee income contributing ₹22,504 crores. However, consolidated ROE declined to 16.89% and ROA to 1.77%.

Asset quality remained exceptional with net NPAs at just 0.33% and ₹11,957 crores held in non-NPA provisions. Gross NPA improved to 1.28% from 1.43%, with provision coverage ratio at 75%. Importantly, the bank avoided RBI divergence disclosure as additional NPAs and provisioning identified fell below the 5% threshold.

Strategic execution focused on the "One Axis" ecosystem and GPS framework across three pillars: Strengthening the Core, Deepening Performance-driven Culture, and Building for the Future. High RAROC segments—Small Business, SME, and Mid-Corporate—grew 14% year-on-year, now representing 23% of the loan book. The bank's subsidiaries performed strongly with combined net worth of ₹10,650 crores (28% growth) and PAT of ₹1,768 crores (11% growth), delivering 46% return on investment of ₹3,812 crores.

The bank demonstrated ESG leadership by exceeding its sustainable wholesale lending target, achieving ₹48,412 crores against the ₹30,000 crore 2026 target, and raising it to ₹60,000 crores by 2030. Through Axis Bank Foundation's Mission 2 Million initiative, the bank impacted 2.05 million households by FY25. The bank maintains 34.5% gender diversity and targets 30% women representation by FY27.

Risk management remained comprehensive despite headwinds including global growth deceleration (IMF revised 2025 growth to 2.8%), trade tensions, and regulatory compliance requirements. The bank faced RBI penalties of ₹1.91 crores for compliance violations and ₹37.33 lakhs for FEMA violations. However, its governance framework—featuring a 13-member Board led by Independent Director N.S. Vishwanathan and enhanced IT governance following RBI guidelines—positioned it in the "Leadership" category of the Indian Corporate Governance Scorecard. The bank operates through 104,000+ employees serving customers across diverse markets while navigating evolving regulatory landscapes including MeitY's DPDP Rules and SEBI's enhanced BRSR norms.

# HDFC Bank FY25 Master Summary

HDFC Bank delivered resilient performance in FY25, its first full year following the landmark merger with HDFC Limited (effective July 1, 2023), transforming into India's leading financial conglomerate. Profit After Tax grew 10.7% to ₹67,347 crore from ₹60,812 crore, while Net Interest Income increased 13.0% to ₹1,22,670 crore. However, profitability metrics moderated with Return on Assets declining to 1.91% from 1.98% and Return on Equity falling to 14.6% from 16.1%. Earnings Per Share reached ₹88.3, and the Board recommended an increased dividend of ₹22.0 per share, representing a 25% payout ratio.

The bank executed a strategic balance sheet recalibration, prioritizing deposit mobilization over loan growth. Deposits surged 14.1% to ₹27,14,715 crore while advances grew deliberately slower at 5.4% to ₹26,19,609 crore, reducing the credit-to-deposit ratio from approximately 110% post-merger to 96% by March 31, 2025. This captured approximately 14.6% of incremental deposit market share and reduced high-cost borrowings to 14% of total funding. The Net Interest Margin stood at 3.48%, with total balance sheet expanding 8.1% to ₹39,10,199 crore.

Asset quality remained industry-leading with Gross NPAs at just 1.33% of gross advances. Capital adequacy strengthened significantly to 19.6% (Tier 1: 17.7%), well above the regulatory minimum of 11.7%, with AAA ratings across instruments. Provisions dropped substantially to ₹11,649 crore from ₹23,492 crore, aided by lower loan loss provisions.

The bank's distribution footprint expanded to 24,854 banking outlets comprising 9,455 branches (51% in semi-urban/rural areas), 21,139 ATMs, and 15,399 business correspondents across 4,150 cities, serving 9.7 crore customers. Digital transformation accelerated dramatically with 97% of financial transactions conducted digitally and 99% of personal loans originated digitally, while the HDFC Bank One platform recorded 3.7 crore monthly customer engagements.

As a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB), governance was strengthened with 53.85% independent directors and a dedicated Group Oversight Department monitoring frameworks across subsidiaries including insurance, mutual funds, and asset management. The bank employed 2,14,521 staff (26.1% women) with investments of 1.25 crore learning hours.

Strategic priorities focused on sustainability with commitment to carbon neutrality by FY32, achieving 18.69% sustainable finance portfolio and 45% reduction in emission intensity. CSR initiative Parivartan spent ₹1,068 crore benefitting over 10 crore people. Management positioned this phase as "HDFC Bank 2.0," emphasizing post-merger integration, AI-enabled customer experiences, and leveraging India's 6.5% economic growth trajectory while navigating global uncertainties and regulatory complexities.

# ICICI Bank FY25 Annual Report: Master Summary

ICICI Bank delivered strong financial performance in FY25, its 70th year since inception, with standalone net profit reaching ₹472.27 billion, representing 15.5% year-on-year growth. Consolidated profit after tax rose 15.3% to ₹510.29 billion. Profit before tax (excluding treasury income) grew 14.9% to ₹626.16 billion, while net interest income increased to ₹811.65 billion. Diluted earnings per share improved to ₹1,052.89 from ₹894.95 in FY24. The Board recommended a dividend of ₹11.00 per equity share.

**Balance Sheet and Capital Position:**
Total assets reached ₹21,182.40 billion, with deposits growing to ₹16,103.48 billion and loans advancing to ₹13,417.66 billion. The deposit composition remained balanced with current accounts at 18.8%, savings accounts at 20.6%, and term deposits at 53.5%. Average current account deposits grew 11.7% while savings accounts increased 10.2% year-over-year. Net worth strengthened to ₹2,920.77 billion. Capital adequacy remained robust with Total CRAR at 19.12%, Tier I at 18.34%, and Common Equity Tier 1 at 17.12%, significantly above regulatory requirements.

**Asset Quality and Business Growth:**
Asset quality improved with gross NPAs declining to ₹241.66 billion (0.4% ratio) from ₹311.84 billion. Net NPA ratio remained stable at 0.4%, reflecting disciplined credit practices. The Business Banking portfolio expanded significantly by 33.7% to ₹2,633.67 billion, contributing 19.6% to net advances. The Bank maintained close to 18 million active credit cards and disbursed loans to 92,595 Self-Help Groups reaching over 1 million women.

**Strategic Initiatives and Digital Transformation:**
A major milestone was the delisting and acquisition of ICICI Securities on March 24, 2025, making it a wholly-owned subsidiary through allotment of 56,008,117 equity shares. Digital platforms scaled significantly with iMobile processing 558 million transactions worth ₹11,238 billion during FY25, while InstaBIZ transaction value surged 37%. The Bank launched technology-driven platforms including SmartLock, iCRM for 360° customer relationship management, and DigiEase for seamless Business Banking onboarding.

**Risk Management and Governance:**
The Bank operates through four independent risk monitoring groups covering Credit Risk, Market Risk, Operational Risk, and Financial Crime Prevention. Industry exposure (excluding retail) is limited to 15% of total portfolio, with concentration risk managed through borrower-specific limits based on internal ratings. The Board underwent significant transitions with Pradeep Kumar Sinha appointed as Non-Executive Part-time Chairman effective July 1, 2024, and two new independent directors joining.

**Sustainability and Social Impact:**
ICICI Bank committed ₹1,800 crore to Tata Memorial Centre and set a carbon neutrality target for Scope 1 and 2 emissions by fiscal 2032. CSR expenditure totaled ₹8,011.2 million, exceeding mandated requirements, with initiatives benefitting an estimated 19 million individuals through ICICI Foundation for Inclusive Growth.

# Kotak Mahindra Bank FY25 Master Summary

Kotak Mahindra Bank delivered strong financial performance in FY25 despite operational challenges, reporting consolidated net profit of ₹22,126 crore (21.5% YoY growth) and maintaining a five-year profit CAGR of 22%. Net Interest Income reached ₹28,342 crore, though Net Interest Margin compressed to 5.0% from 5.3% in FY24. On a standalone basis, net profit was ₹16,450 crore, including a ₹3,013 crore gain from divesting 70% of Kotak Mahindra General Insurance. Basic earnings per share improved to ₹111.3 from ₹91.5, while book value per share grew 21% to ₹792.

The bank's balance sheet strengthened considerably, with consolidated assets reaching ₹879,774 crore. Total advances grew 13% YoY to ₹486,166 crore, and deposits expanded to ₹499,055 crore (16% CAGR), though CASA ratio declined to 43.0% from 45.5%, reflecting industry-wide pressure on low-cost deposits. Capital position remained robust with a Capital Adequacy Ratio of 23.3% and CET1 of 22.3%, well above regulatory requirements. Asset quality stayed exceptional with Gross NPA at 1.4% and Net NPA at 0.3-0.4%. Return on Equity improved to 15.2% while Return on Average Assets held at 2.7%. Market capitalization reached ₹431,683 crore with a P/E of 19.5x.

The bank operates through four business engines across 2,148 branches, 3,295 ATMs, and international offices in six locations, serving over 5.3 crore customers with 114,000 employees. Assets under management totaled ₹669,885 crore, with relationship value exceeding ₹920,000 crore in private and priority banking segments.

A significant challenge emerged when RBI imposed restrictions on digital customer onboarding and credit card issuance, which were lifted in February 2025 after comprehensive remediation. Additionally, the microfinance sector downturn required operational adjustments. Despite these headwinds, net customer complaints declined 28% year-over-year.

The bank embedded ESG principles across operations, conducting enhanced materiality assessments identifying 18 material topics. Critical risk areas include data security (ISO/IEC 27001 certified), regulatory compliance (PCI DSS 4.0 implemented), and cybersecurity. The bank reported zero disciplinary actions for bribery or corruption and conducted over 250,000 training hours for fraud prevention and 1 million hours on anti-corruption policies.

Governance remained strong with 55% independent directors, 27% gender diversity, and 95% Board meeting attendance. Strategic initiatives focused on digital transformation through persona-based apps, enhanced corporate banking platforms, and new propositions like Solitaire for affluent customers, targeting advances growth at 1.5-2x nominal GDP while maintaining strict risk management standards.

# State Bank of India FY25 Master Summary

State Bank of India delivered robust financial performance in FY25 despite challenging global conditions, with net profit surging 16.08% to ₹70,901 crore from ₹61,077 crore in FY24. Operating profit grew 17.89% to ₹1,10,579 crore, while net interest income increased 4.43% to ₹1,66,965 crore and other income jumped 19.35% to ₹61,683 crore. Return on assets improved to 1.10% from 1.04%, with return on equity at 19.87%. Earnings per share reached ₹79.44, up from ₹68.44, demonstrating strong shareholder value creation.

**Balance Sheet and Market Position:**
Total assets expanded 8.03% to ₹66,76,053 crore, with the bank maintaining dominant market shares of 22.54% in deposits and 19.36% in advances. Deposits grew 9.48% to ₹53,82,190 crore, while net advances increased robustly at 12.40% to ₹41,63,312 crore. The CASA ratio stood at 39.97%, with current account deposits surging 27.02%. The retail advances portfolio crossed ₹15 lakh crore (41.8% of domestic advances), while corporate advances grew 16.43% YoY, driven by NBFCs, infrastructure, and renewable energy sectors.

**Asset Quality and Capital Strength:**
Asset quality showed significant improvement, with gross NPA declining to 1.82% from 2.24% and net NPA dropping to 0.47% from 0.57%. Absolute gross NPAs fell to ₹76,880 crore from ₹84,276 crore, with provision coverage ratio at 92.08%. Major NPA concentration remains in power, telecom, infrastructure, agriculture (38% of total), and personal segments (14%). The bank approved 524 liquidation cases through NCLT and pursues recovery through NARCL/ARC transfers. Capital adequacy stood comfortable at 14.25% (Tier-I: 12.11%), exceeding the additional 0.80% CET1 requirement as a D-SIB effective April 2025.

**Strategic Initiatives and Global Presence:**
SBI raised over USD 3.6 billion in long-term resources, including $3.07 billion for green financing and $1.05 billion through green bonds, targeting 7.5% green portfolio of domestic advances by 2030. The bank operates 22,937 branches and 63,791 ATMs domestically, with 244 overseas offices across 29 countries. Digital transformation continues with 8.77 crore YONO customers processing 220 million daily UPI transactions. ESG performance improved significantly with MSCI ratings升级 from BBB to A and DJSI scores rising from 37 to 49.

**Risk Environment:**
Operating in a challenging global environment with IMF projecting 2.8% growth in 2025 and inflation declining to 4.3%, SBI faces headwinds from trade fragmentation and restrictive policies. Total provisions increased 54.87% to ₹39,679 crore, reflecting conservative risk management. The bank maintains strong credit ratings (Moody's: Baa3/Stable, S&P and Fitch: BBB-) and comprehensive risk frameworks covering credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks through RAROC methodology for advances ₹5 crore and above.
